title: Independent whole-repository architecture and AI-operating-model audit
goal: Obtain a read-only independent deep review of the entire TIA Automation Factory repository, including product architecture, Siemens/TIA boundaries, code quality, tests, workflows, AI collaboration model, prompts, review/repair mechanics, documentation consistency and development methodology; produce prioritized recommendations and improved prompt drafts without modifying the repository.
scope: Read-only audit of the entire repository and live GitHub state: source, tests, docs, tasks, agents, workflows, reviews, issues, PRs and relevant Actions evidence.
Evaluate the production goal and architecture from vendor-neutral automation model through PLC IR, Siemens SCL/Open Library integration and trusted TIA Portal V21 Openness execution.
Audit agents/prompts/*.md, agent runtime/context construction, reviewer protocol and human/AI interaction for correctness, efficiency, autonomy and unnecessary ceremony.
Propose complete replacement drafts for coder, repair and reviewer prompts where improvement is justified; preserve trust boundaries rather than weakening them for convenience.
Identify contradictions, stale snapshots, duplicated policy, over-engineering, missing tests, security/trust risks and places where the human is unnecessarily used as a message bus.
Do not modify files, open PRs, execute candidate code on Windows/TIA, access secrets/vendor payloads or touch IndustrialMDE.

requirements: Report binds itself to the audited default-branch SHA and names the live PR/issues/Actions state used.
Separates observed facts, inferences and recommendations.
States what is already strong and should be preserved, not only defects.
Ranks findings by critical/major/minor and cites concrete repository evidence.
Includes architecture, code/test, CI/CD, TIA/Open Library, security/trust, documentation, methodology and AI-agent/prompt analysis.
Includes complete proposed prompt text for coder, repair, requirements/code reviewer and PLC/TIA reviewer, plus recommendations for primary-orchestrator instructions if needed.
Includes a simplification analysis: controls to keep, controls to automate, controls to remove/defer, and how to minimize human copying/manual routing.
Produces a prioritized action plan that distinguishes immediate blockers from improvements that must not delay generator development.
tia: No Windows/TIA execution is required; existing trusted TIA evidence may be reviewed read-only.
